svg.text: FORMAT LINEAGE: Alex Xu / ByteByteGo format • MCP specification
How MCP Actually Works: 9 Messages From 'User Asks' to 'Tool Result in Context'
ByteByteGo-style walkthrough of the Model Context Protocol — the open standard (Nov 2024) behind most agent tool connectors. JSON-RPC 2.0 under the hood.
Claude Desktop, an IDE, or your own agent (Google ADK / LangGraph)
lives inside the host; speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 to one server
GitHub, PostgreSQL, filesystem, your internal API
host decides a tool may help
ask what the server can do
tool schemas (name, description, JSON input schema)
host puts the schemas in the model's context
after user consent if the host requires it
server ran the real API or query
result enters context → model answers the user
treat it as untrusted data, not instructions
stdio for local servers (the IDE launches the process); Streamable
HTTP for remote servers behind auth.
Servers expose tools, resources, prompts. Servers can ask the client
for sampling (an LLM call) or elicitation (ask the user).
Tool results are untrusted content. Mixing a server that reads
private data with one that sends messages creates Willison's lethal
Open source clients: MCP Python/TypeScript SDKs • Google ADK MCPToolset • LangChain MCP adapters — same nine messages everywhere.
Curated by Nitin Aggarwal • Google Cloud ADK + OpenHands Factory • Proprietary + Confidential
modelcontextprotocol.io specification: lifecycle, tools, resources, prompts, sampling, transports
